standard.title: Sensory and functional food properties for healthy eating
standard.description: analyse and make judgements on how the sensory and functional properties of food influence the design and preparation of sustainable food solutions for healthy eating
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can analyse how the properties of foods determine their preparation and presentation techniques, and how health, food safety and sustainability affect food choices (AC9TDE8K05). They can identify sensory and nutritional properties of food. They have not yet made judgements on how these properties interact in designing sustainable food solutions, nor examined food preservation, trend-driven food innovation, or emerging food technologies.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and make judgements on how sensory and functional food properties influence the design and preparation of sustainable food solutions for healthy eating — including food preservation, trends, and emerging technologies.

nodes.label: Sensory and nutritional assessment of food
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can conduct or interpret sensory and nutritional assessments of foods and explain how these characteristics inform food solution design.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two sensory characteristics (e.g. texture, flavour, colour, aroma) and explain how they influence a food design decision.
nodes.typical_width: Conduct or interpret sensory and nutritional assessments across a range of foods; explain how sensory characteristics (flavour, texture, colour, aroma) and nutritional properties interact; use assessment findings to inform decisions about food solution design.
wider: Compare freshly squeezed juice with commercial alternatives through sensory and nutritional assessment — make a judgement on which better serves a healthy eating solution and explain the trade-offs
Analyse how First Nations Australians' understanding of detoxification processes (e.g. cycad nuts) reflects sophisticated knowledge of the functional properties of food
Compare locally grown with imported produce through sensory assessment — evaluate how freshness, seasonality and food miles interact in sustainable food solution design

response_modes.reason: Sensory assessment requires precision and consistent application of criteria — colour, texture, flavour and aroma each need to be identified and described reliably. Sufficient practice with varied foods builds the assessment fluency that N3 evaluation requires.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two sensory characteristics and explains how each affects food quality or acceptability
Connects assessment findings to a design decision — not just describes the food
nodes.hinge_reason: Sensory and nutritional assessment skills established at N1 are applied at N3 when evaluating food trends — students who cannot conduct or interpret assessments cannot judge whether innovations improve nutritional value or sensory quality.

nodes.label: Food preservation and spoilage
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how food spoilage occurs and how preservation methods affect food structure, sensory properties and nutritional value.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe one cause of food spoilage and one preservation method; explain how the preservation method changes the food's properties.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how different causes of food spoilage (microbial, enzymatic, oxidative) are addressed by different preservation methods; analyse how methods such as freezing, dehydrating, or heat treatment affect food structure, sensory properties and nutritional value; apply safe food handling and storage principles including danger-zone temperatures.
wider: Experiment with dehydration and compare the sensory and nutritional properties of the fresh and dehydrated product — make a judgement on when dehydration is a suitable preservation method

Evaluate multiple preservation methods for the same food against criteria of safety, nutritional retention, sensory quality and sustainability — make a judgement on the best approach for a specific food solution context
Develop a comprehensive food safety checklist for a food service context — explain how each element addresses a specific spoilage or contamination risk

response_modes.reason: Food safety knowledge requires precision — danger-zone temperatures, contamination vectors, storage requirements. Students need sufficient practice applying these accurately before they can make judgements about preservation method trade-offs. Errors in food safety knowledge have real consequences.

success_criteria: Correctly identifies at least one spoilage mechanism and the preservation method that addresses it
Explains how the preservation method changes at least one food property (sensory or nutritional)
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot identify spoilage causes and preservation responses cannot design food solutions at N3 that are both safe and aligned with food trends — the food safety requirement runs through all food solution design.

nodes.label: Food trends and sustainable healthy eating
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse food trends and evaluate how they influence food solution design for healthy eating and sustainability.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one current food trend and explain how it might influence the design of a food solution for healthy eating.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse multiple food trends (e.g. plant-based foods, organic ingredients, insect protein, non-dairy milk, food delivery) and evaluate how each influences food solution design — considering health, sustainability and practicality; make a judgement on which trends genuinely advance healthy and sustainable eating.
wider: Evaluate the health and sustainability claims of two competing food trends (e.g. plant-based meat vs conventional protein, non-dairy milk vs dairy) — make a judgement grounded in nutritional and environmental evidence

Investigate how innovations in food technology (e.g. 3D food printing, IoT food supply chain, AR food labelling) may influence future food solution design — evaluate the potential benefits and risks for healthy eating

Design a healthy canteen item that incorporates a current food trend — document how sensory, nutritional and sustainability considerations shaped the design and use food photography and digital promotion tools

response_modes.reason: Food trends vary enormously in their health and sustainability basis — some are well-evidenced, others are marketing-driven. Students who evaluate only one trend cannot develop the analytical framework for distinguishing trend from evidence. Multiple contrasting trends — each with different health and sustainability profiles — build this judgement capacity.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparative evaluation of competing food trend claims is rich — it requires students to engage with nutritional science, environmental evidence, and commercial framing simultaneously, and the judgement is genuinely non-trivial.
success_criteria: Identifies a specific food trend and connects it to both healthy eating and sustainability considerations
Makes a judgement — not just a description — about the trend's merits and limitations
